_comment: THE BUILDER REPORT. The second of the two documents about a person: the session card
says what just happened, and this says how they build and whether it is changing.
NOTHING IN HERE IS WRITTEN BY A MODEL. Every field is a number this machine measured,
which is why there is no JSON Schema output and no `stamped` rule: there is no
constrained decoder to constrain and no claim to take back. What the spec buys is the
same thing it buys everywhere else — one definition, three notations, and a door the
server can close with `extra='forbid'` on a document it did not compute.
scripts/gen_report.py emits, both committed, both `git diff --exit-code`'d in CI:
server/builder/report_spec.py     Pydantic, extra='forbid', on the way into Postgres
mobile/src/generated/report.ts    what the profile screen renders
WHY THE SERVER CANNOT COMPUTE IT. Three of the five blocks rest on things that never
leave the machine (privacy/upload-contract.json): subagent sidecar transcripts, shell
command text, and prompt text. The server has counts, not commands, so it can no more
compute `quality` than it can compute the narrative.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. `analysis/rules.py` produces CLAUDE.md lines from ERROR
TEXT, which carries paths and file names; it stays on the machine and is written to a
file there. `analysis/playbook.py` splits PROMPTS, so only its counts travel and not one
word of a prompt. Every field below is a number, a date, a metric name or a label from
a fixed table in this repository.
NULL IS NOT ZERO, everywhere in this document. A block is null when it was refused, and
the refusal carries its reason so the phone can say why instead of drawing an empty
chart. A `reason` beside a null number is the difference between 'we do not know' and
'it was nothing'.

ReportTrend.name: metric
ReportTrend.doc: the metric's key, from analysis/profile.py. Stable across versions; the label is not.

ReportTrend.name: label
ReportTrend.doc: the metric in words a person reads, from the one table in analysis/trends.py.

ReportTrend.name: before
ReportTrend.doc: its value over the older of the two equal windows.

ReportTrend.name: now
ReportTrend.doc: its value over the newer window.

ReportTrend.name: move
ReportTrend.doc: the signed relative change, (now - before) / before. 0.7 is up 70 percent.

ReportTrend.name: direction
ReportTrend.doc: up, down, or steady. Steady is a real answer: under the noise floor is not a move.

ReportTrend.name: good
ReportTrend.doc: whether this direction is the one they want, when the metric has a direction at all. Null means the change is reported with no verdict: more hours is not better and a night owl is not broken.

ReportTrend.name: sessions_before
ReportTrend.doc: sittings in the older window. Both windows need a sample or there is no trend.

ReportAgentType.name: name
ReportAgentType.doc: the subagent type as the harness names it: general-purpose, Explore, workflow-subagent.

ReportAgentType.name: agents
ReportAgentType.doc: how many instances of that type ran.

ReportAgents.name: agents
ReportAgents.doc: subagent instances that ran in the window. Counted from sidecar transcripts, which every other tool skips.

ReportAgents.name: produced
ReportAgents.doc: how many of them did anything at all: a tool call, a file, an error. An agent that produced nothing is a delegation that cost tokens and returned air.

ReportAgents.name: max_concurrent
ReportAgents.doc: the most that were running at the same moment. A handoff is not two agents at once, so an end sorts before a start at equal timestamps.

ReportAgents.name: agent_seconds
ReportAgents.doc: the sum of every agent's own span. Deliberately larger than wall time when they overlap; that overlap is the point.

ReportAgents.name: wall_seconds
ReportAgents.doc: clock time from the first agent starting to the last one stopping.

ReportAgents.name: busy_seconds
ReportAgents.doc: how much of that stretch had at least one agent running. The union of the spans, so an overlap counts once.

ReportAgents.name: parallelism
ReportAgents.doc: agent_seconds over busy_seconds: while agents were running, how many were running at once. 1.0 is a queue, 3.4 is three and a bit at a time. Never below 1.0 when anything ran, which is why the denominator is the union and not the stretch.

ReportAgents.name: by_type
ReportAgents.doc: the split by subagent type, most common first.

ReportDay.name: day
ReportDay.doc: the day, YYYY-MM-DD, with the 04:00 boundary this repository uses everywhere else.

ReportDay.name: assisted
ReportDay.doc: commits that landed while an agent was working.

ReportDay.name: alone
ReportDay.doc: commits that landed outside every session window. Deliberately generous: anything the capture never saw counts here.

ReportContributions.name: assisted
ReportContributions.doc: commits with an agent in the room.

ReportContributions.name: alone
ReportContributions.doc: commits you wrote on your own.

ReportContributions.name: active_days
ReportContributions.doc: days you shipped something. Not days you opened the app: a streak a tab can extend is a streak about the tab.

ReportContributions.name: longest_streak
ReportContributions.doc: the longest run of consecutive shipping days.

ReportContributions.name: current_streak
ReportContributions.doc: the run ending today or yesterday. Yesterday still counts, because today is not over.

ReportContributions.name: days
ReportContributions.doc: one entry per day that had a commit, oldest first. Days with none are absent rather than zero rows.

ReportGreen.name: n
ReportGreen.doc: how many times a failing test run was followed by a passing one.

ReportGreen.name: median_seconds
ReportGreen.doc: the median of those recoveries. The solo builder's answer to DORA's mean time to restore.

ReportGreen.name: median_attempts
ReportGreen.doc: how many runs it typically took to get back to green.

ReportQuality.name: runs
ReportQuality.doc: test runs seen in the window, counted from shell commands.

ReportQuality.name: passed
ReportQuality.doc: runs with no error after them.

ReportQuality.name: first_try_rate
ReportQuality.doc: the share of test runs that were already green. Not 'the first try worked' per feature, which nothing here can see.

ReportQuality.name: time_to_green
ReportQuality.doc: the recovery numbers, or null when nothing in the window failed and then passed.

ReportQuality.name: reason
ReportQuality.doc: why the rates are null, when they are. Present only on a refusal.

ReportPrompting.name: attempts
ReportPrompting.doc: prompts long enough to be an instruction rather than a nudge.

ReportPrompting.name: clean
ReportPrompting.doc: of those, how many landed something without a correction and without the agent stalling.

ReportPrompting.name: costly
ReportPrompting.doc: how many cost a correction or a long stall.

ReportPrompting.name: clean_share
ReportPrompting.doc: clean over attempts. NO PROMPT TEXT TRAVELS: this is the whole of what the playbook uploads.

ReportPrompting.name: reason
ReportPrompting.doc: why the share is null, when it is.

ReportLanguage.name: name
ReportLanguage.doc: the language, from a fixed table of extensions. `other` is an extension nobody mapped, counted rather than guessed at.

ReportLanguage.name: lines
ReportLanguage.doc: lines the agent added in it.

ReportLanguage.name: files
ReportLanguage.doc: distinct files. A count, never a name: paths do not leave the machine.

ReportLanguage.name: share
ReportLanguage.doc: its share of the attributable lines.

ReportLanguages.name: lines
ReportLanguages.doc: attributable lines in the window, generated files already excluded.

ReportLanguages.name: generated_lines_excluded
ReportLanguages.doc: lines nobody wrote: lockfiles, `node_modules`, this repository's own generated Swift, TypeScript and Python. Reported rather than hidden, because a silent exclusion is indistinguishable from a parser that missed the file.

ReportLanguages.name: languages
ReportLanguages.doc: most lines first, the tail summed into `other`. Null when there were too few attributable lines to split.

ReportLanguages.name: reason
ReportLanguages.doc: why the split is null, when it is.

fields.name: report_version
fields.doc: the spec version these rules came from. A retuned threshold is a recompute, not a migration.

fields.name: generated_at
fields.doc: when this was computed. A report describes a corpus as it stood.

fields.name: window_days
fields.doc: how far back the blocks below look.

fields.name: trend_headline
fields.doc: the one sentence version of the trends, phrased to match the window. Null when nothing moved enough to say.

fields.name: trends
fields.doc: you against you, two equal windows back to back. Never a window against all of history, which would report the trend of the corpus growing.

fields.name: agents
fields.doc: how many agents you ran and how much of it was at once. Null when no sidecar transcripts were found, which is the normal state for someone who has never delegated.

fields.name: contributions
fields.doc: commits split by whether an agent was in the room. Null below the minimum, never zero.

fields.name: quality
fields.doc: the two of DORA's four questions a transcript can answer. Null when no repository was resolved.

fields.name: prompting
fields.doc: how often a prompt lands cleanly, and nothing else. Null when neither pile has enough in it to be a rate.

fields.name: languages
fields.doc: what you actually build in, by lines the agent added. Null when no session in the window had a countable write.
